title: Tenali Raman Tale 73 (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: A cunning alchemist named Rasavadi Someshwar arrived at the court of Vijayanagara, claiming he had discovered the legendary Philosopher’s... [KN]
full_text:
A cunning alchemist named Rasavadi Someshwar arrived at the court of Vijayanagara, claiming he had discovered the legendary Philosopher’s Stone (*Sparshamani*).
Before the King and the ministers, he produced a heavy iron rod.
He dipped the tip of the rod into a bubbling crucible of sulfur and mercury, chanted a secret mantra, and pulled it out:
To the astonishment of the King, the tip of the rod had turned into glittering, solid twenty-four-karat gold!

The King was dazzled: 'Someshwar, canst thou turn all the iron in our armory into gold?'
The alchemist bowed: 'Easily, Your Majesty! But the alchemical reaction requires a catalytic seed fund: you must provide me with five thousand gold coins to purchase the rare Himalayan herbs necessary for the grand transmutation!'

King Krishnadevaraya ordered the treasury to prepare the gold.
Tenali Raman stepped forward:
'Maharaj, before we surrender five thousand gold coins, let me examine the miraculous iron rod.'

Tenali took the rod. He tapped it with a steel hammer, scratched the surface, and smiled.
Tenali said to the alchemist:
'Master Someshwar, your alchemy is magnificent! But why spend five thousand gold coins on distant herbs?
Since your iron rod already possesses the golden touch, let us perform the Reverse Transmutation Test!'

Tenali walked to the palace blacksmith’s forge, picked up a heavy pair of blacksmith’s shears, and cleanly snapped the iron rod in two!
He held up the cross-section before the King:
The iron rod was hollow!
Inside the hollow core, the alchemist had concealed a solid gold cylinder, capped with a thin layer of black wax!
When the tip was heated in the crucible, the wax melted, exposing the pre-existing gold inside!

Tenali smiled:
'Behold the Philosopher’s Stone! The only transmutation taking place was the transmutation of the King’s gold into the swindler’s pocket!'

The alchemist fell to the floor, trembling in terror, confessing his fraud.
King Krishnadevaraya was furious at the deception: he confiscated the alchemist’s tools, banished him from the empire, and awarded the solid gold cylinder to Tenali Raman.
Tenali bowed, reminding the court that real wealth is forged by honest human hands, not by alchemical parlor tricks.
moral: Greedy charlatans who claim to transmute base metals into gold are undone when held to their own alchemical claims. [KN]
